newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq criticises U.N. for entering churches.
newsitem.headline: Iraq criticises U.N. for entering churches.

text.p: Iraq said on Wednesday a U.N. arms inspection team had committed a "flagrant aggression" by entering churches and monasteries on the outskirts of Baghdad.

"One of the U.N. Special Commission (UNSCOM) inspection teams has committed today...a flagrant aggression against the Chaldean Mar Paulis church and al-Ibtdaa' and al-Sanabul monasteries for nuns in al-Za'franiya area in Baghdad," the Iraqi News Agency (INA) said.
UNSCOM is in charge of destroying Iraq's weapons of mass destruction under the U.N. Security Council's terms of the 1991 Gulf War ceasefire.
The U.N. will lift curbs on Iraqi oil exports, imposed for Iraq's 1990 invasion of Kuwait, once UNSCOM says Baghdad has no prohibited weapons any more.
"We strongly condemn this action and urge...all those of good-will to try to put an end to such behaviour and work for ending the embargo," it said.
